claim: Subspace capture has a sparsity sweet spot
published: restricted R² (k_i atoms reconstruct each manifold from superposed codes) peaks near k = 4 (Bhalla et al. 2026, Fig. 4A)
ours: mean restricted R² peaks at k = 6 (0.53; 0.42 at k = 3, 0.48 at k = 25); regime label 'capture' for up to 100% of 48 manifolds
criterion: restricted-R² peak at k ∈ {3, 4, 6} (amendment 2026-11-27: the paper's capture score; was 'capture fraction')
post_hoc: metric switched to restricted R² after a full run whose log showed its peak

claim: Sparsity moves the SAE from shattering (small k) to dilution (large k)
published: low k: shattered across atoms; intermediate k: capture; high k: redundant atoms lose specificity (dilution) (Fig. 4B)
ours: shattering 0% at k = 3 → 0% at k = 25; dilution 0% → 100%
criterion: dilution at the largest k ≥ 30 points above the smallest k and shattering higher at the smallest k (amendment: the pre-stated claim had the direction reversed relative to the paper)
post_hoc: claim restated (direction corrected) after a full run

claim: Confirmatory: subspace capture has an interior sparsity optimum (fresh seeds)
published: restricted R² peaks near k = 4 (Bhalla et al. 2026, Fig. 4A)
ours: k* = 6 on 3 selection seeds; on 3 held-out seeds R²(k*) − max(R²(3), R²(25)) = 0.075 [0.034, 0.121] (95% CI, seeds × instances); held-out R² by k: k=3: 0.42, k=4: 0.50, k=6: 0.54, k=8: 0.51, k=10: 0.51, k=14: 0.50, k=20: 0.48, k=25: 0.47. Originally pre-stated metric: capture fraction peaks at k = 3 (max 100%)
criterion: k* ∈ {4, 6} and CI of Δ > 0; partial if k* ∈ {8, …, 20} and CI > 0 (pre-stated 2026-11-28)

claim: Confirmatory: low k shatters, high k dilutes (fresh seeds)
published: low k: shattering; high k: dilution (Fig. 4B)
ours: held-out seeds: dilution rises by 99 points [94, 100] from k = 3 to 25; shattering drops by 0 points
criterion: dilution rise ≥ 30 points with CI > 0 and shattering drop > 0; partial if both > 0 (pre-stated 2026-11-28)
